text: {"domains":{"block_M":[16,32],"block_N":[64,128,256],"block_K":[64,128],"num_stages":[2,3,4],"threads":[128,256],"swizzle":[0,4,8,16,32,64]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":0.3,"launches":1.5,"pipeline":1,"footprint":1},"rationale":"History: attempts 00/02 (M=32,N=64,K=32,st=3) both ~195.8us; 01 (M=16,N=64,K=64,st=2,thr=256) 176.4us; 03 (M=32,N=64,K=64,st=2,thr=256,sw=64) 147.68us best; 04 (same but thr=128) 147.67us, essentially tied. Signals: DRAM identical at 33.8 MB across swizzle variants, so panel-reuse proxy gives no measured locality at M/block_M<=2 -> keep traffic low (0.3). block_K=32 lost twice (dropped); K={64,128} retained since K=64 clearly helped. block_M={16,32} only (M=32; 64/128 overshoot and never won). Stages={2,3,4}: stage=4 still untested and now prioritized per instructions. Threads: 128 vs 256 tied at the best tuple, so both retained to test the changed-thread hypothesis against a wider-N/K=128/stage=4 tuple. Swizzle full domain kept but low traffic weight so it cannot dominate; if a swizzle variant again reproduces flat DRAM/latency we further cut it. shared_memory_limit stays 32768 (hard portability cap binds anyway); footprint weight 1 penalizes stage=4+K=128+N=256 under the cap. Next hypothesis: test block_K=128 with stage>=3 and/or block_N=128/256 against the 147.7us winner to see if deeper K/stages or wider N beats the current best; GB10 values are simulator estimates (not hardware), Metal validates exact source/TIR numerically but CUDA binary is not executed; no global optimality claimed."}
